title_zh: 校园与学习模拟卷（四篇完整听力）
instruction_zh: 听录音，完成第 1–40 题。每题填空不超过 TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER；选择类题目选 A/B/C 或配对项字母。
audio_text: Good morning, city library, this is Anna speaking. Hello, I am a new student at the university and I want to join the library. Welcome, the joining process is very simple and it takes about ten minutes. First, please fill in the registration form on our website. You will need your student card number and a recent photo. After that, we will send you a library card by post within five working days. How many books can I borrow at one time? Students may borrow up to twelve books for three weeks. Can I renew them if I have not finished reading? Yes, you can renew each book twice, either online or by telephone. Is there a quiet reading room on the ground floor? Yes, the silent reading room is open from eight in the morning until nine at night. Are food and drink allowed in the reading room? Only water in a closed bottle is permitted, and no hot food. Thank you very much, I will register online this afternoon. By the way, is there a computer room for students on the first floor? Yes, there are forty computers and they can be booked for two hours at a time. Printing is available on every floor, but you need to bring your own paper. The library also runs a free reading club for international students every Thursday. You can find the timetable on the notice board near the main entrance. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the campus history talk. My name is Professor Hughes, and I will describe the early years of this university. The university was founded in 1892 by a group of local teachers and merchants. The first building, the Old Hall, was completed in 1895 and still stands today. At that time, there were only forty students and six teachers. The library began as a single room in the Old Hall with just two hundred books. During the first world war, the campus was used as a hospital for wounded soldiers. After the war, the university grew quickly and new departments were created. The science block was opened in 1928, thanks to a generous donation from a former student. By 1950, the student population had reached two thousand. The famous clock tower was added in 1963 to celebrate the university's seventy first anniversary. In the 1970s, the campus expanded to the east side of the river. Today, the university has more than twenty thousand students from over eighty countries. The Old Hall is now a museum and is open to visitors every weekend. If you would like to see the museum, please meet me at the main entrance at three o'clock. The university archive holds photographs and letters from the early years. Researchers can visit the archive by appointment on weekday mornings. A new digital collection of old exam papers was launched last month. The oldest item in the collection is a student notebook from 1893. It records lectures in Latin, which was a required subject at the time. The museum shop sells postcards, greeting cards, notebooks, books, posters, mugs, pens, magnets and small souvenirs. Guided tours for school groups can be arranged through the museum office. Thank you for your attention, and I hope you enjoy the rest of the day. Hi Tom, have you finished the group project for the economics course? Not yet, I have only written the introduction and the first section. I am still collecting data for the survey about student spending habits. How many people have you asked so far? I have interviewed about thirty students in the canteen this week. That is good progress, I have only asked fifteen so far. What software are you using to analyse the results? I am using a simple spreadsheet, and it works quite well. Have you written the conclusion yet? No, I will write it after I finish analysing the data. When is the project due? The deadline is next Friday at five o'clock in the afternoon. Shall we meet tomorrow to compare our work? Yes, let us meet in the study room at two o'clock. Bring your laptop and I will bring the printed charts. Do we need to prepare a presentation for the project? Yes, each group will give a ten minute talk in the last seminar. I will make slides for the talk, and you can check them tonight. The tutor said we should include at least five different charts. We can use the computer lab in the evening if the classroom is free. I will book a room online and send you the confirmation. Let us also prepare some questions in case the audience asks about our method. Good idea, I will write down three possible questions and answers. Then we are ready, I will see you tomorrow at two. Welcome to the university careers centre, I am Sarah, the careers adviser. The centre helps students find internships, part time jobs and graduate positions. We are open from nine to five, Monday to Friday, and no appointment is needed. On our website, you can search for jobs by industry, location and salary range. We also offer free workshops on writing CVs and preparing for interviews. The next CV workshop takes place on Tuesday at three in the afternoon. If you want individual advice, you can book a twenty minute session with an adviser. Many companies visit the campus in the autumn to meet final year students. The careers fair will be held in the main hall on the fifteenth of November. Last year, more than one hundred companies attended the fair. We also have a database of alumni who are willing to mentor current students. You can join the mentoring programme by filling in a short online form. Remember to bring your student card when you visit the centre. If you have any questions, please ask at the reception desk. Thank you for listening, and we hope to see you at the centre soon. The centre also publishes a monthly newsletter with job listings and deadlines. You can subscribe to the newsletter by email through the website. We strongly recommend that final year students visit the centre before the end of October. Many graduate schemes close their applications before the Christmas holidays. The adviser can also help you write a personal statement for a scholarship. There is a quiet room where you can make telephone calls to employers. If you are interested in starting your own business, we run a special workshop every month. The workshop covers writing a business plan, finding investors and registering a company.
